analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a new section (head lines 173-190) 'Close codes and the reconnect wait'. The section says the provider reads the WebSocket close code, not the reason, and waits differently after code 1012 (service restart, delay drawn from serviceRestartDelayRange, backoff not grown) than after any other close, where the backoff grows. A session open for stableSessionDuration or longer resets the backoff, and every reconnect sends a fresh register.

No code, key handling, attestation, encryption or authorization path changes. The reconnect wait lives in provider-swift CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift, which was not supplied, so I could not verify the described behavior. The coordinator is trusted in this threat model, so a coordinator-chosen 1012 only affects provider availability. A malicious coordinator-side party that can force closes would be outside the model. The documented rule that every reconnect sends a fresh register is consistent with the TB-002/TB-011 endpoint-resumption and fresh-attestation assumptions. The documentation states no weakened trust, and nothing suggests 1012 skips re-registration or reuses grants.

The base excerpts (lines 951-1229 and 1230-1546) are the unchanged surrounding context: model replace, prefix_cache v2, prompt_work, GLM contract, autopilot, and the like. They are not touched by this PR. The existing T-041 and cache receipt text is unchanged, as are the TB-011 App Attest authorization semantics.

I identified no security regression and no threat-model gap. The only open item is an integration check that CoordinatorReconnectPolicy matches the doc, specifically that 1012 never bypasses register or attestation. That is documentation accuracy, not a finding.
